about: English for XHlp help entries that are not word-for-word copies of a spirit, skill, ability or part description. tools/merge_help.py copies the rest from descriptions.json and writes the full XHlp table there. Icon names used here must match the icon English: battle icons ATK CTR SUP SIM SHP AST EVA DEF (WND.BIN), status icons STA WPN MOB ARM HP MOV DIS (WND.BIN), and the text markers Su As Ph Pi Nu We (boot_ui.json).
3: The number of units that can sortie.
4: The number of stages cleared so far.
5: The current scene. A scene is made up of several stages.
6: The pilot's level. Leveling up raises the pilot's stats, and can teach new Spirit Commands or raise skill levels.

27: Parts equipped / max parts the unit can equip.

72: The pilot's evasive ability. The higher it is, the more easily the pilot evades attacks.
73: The pilot's shooting ability. The higher it is, the more damage ranged weapons deal.

81: The weapon's name. ㍉ marks melee, ㌦ melee-ranged and ㌧ ranged weapons.

83: The value added to the hit rate when this weapon is used.
84: Whether the weapon can be used after the unit moves.
85: "M" marks MAP weapons, "As" marks Assist Attack weapons.
86: Whether the weapon can Double Attack. If it can, it hits the target and an adjacent unit at the same time.
87: "B" marks beam weapons, "G" gravity weapons and "Ph" physical weapons.
88: Whether the weapon can spread or pierce. Spread defeats After Image; pierce halves shield effects and wears shields down 1 more than usual.
89: "Nu" nullifies all barriers. "Pi" nullifies and "We" halves barriers other than the AT Field. "A" nullifies the AT Field.
90: Whether the weapon is electronically guided. Guided weapons have no effect on targets with the Jammer ability.
91: Whether the weapon can destroy buildings.
93: The main pilot Will needed to use this weapon; the main pilot's current Will is in brackets. Without enough Will it cannot be used.
94: The weapon's critical bonus. The higher it is, the more often critical hits happen.
95: The EN this weapon uses; the current EN is in brackets. Without enough EN it cannot be used.
96: The pilot skill needed to use this weapon. Pilots without that skill cannot use it.
97: The extra effect this weapon has on the target.
98: The weapon's accuracy, added to the hit rate when it is used.
99: Suitability for each terrain: S, A, B, C or -. S suits the terrain best.
100: Whether the weapon can be used after the unit moves.
101: MAP weapons hit several enemies at once. Assist weapons add an extra attack when an adjacent unit makes an Assist Attack.
102: Whether the weapon can Double Attack. If it can, it hits the target and an adjacent unit at the same time.
103: Whether the weapon is a beam, gravity or physical weapon.
104: Whether the weapon can spread or pierce. Spread defeats After Image; pierce halves shield effects and wears shields down 1 more than usual.
105: "Nullify" nullifies all barriers. "Pierce" nullifies and "Weaken" halves barriers other than the AT Field. "Nullify AT" nullifies the AT Field.
106: Whether the weapon can destroy buildings.
107: Spirit Commands active on the pilot.
108: ST: pilot stats down, WP: weapon hit down, MB: Mobility down, AR: Armor down, HP: HP down, MV: Move down, DS: the unit cannot act.

110: How much this terrain lowers the hit rate of attacks against a unit on it.

120: SUP, SIM and SHP: supporting units. AST: assisting units. W: Double Attack target. ATK: main unit. CTR, DEF and EVA: the response. Small icons use the first letters (SP, SM, SH, AS, AT, CT, DF, EV).
